title: test(scripts): census why the push-lane coverage gate was red, by cause
body:
Fixes #8545

**This card is a measurement, not a remedy.** Nothing here changes a threshold, a
timeout, a shard count, a coverage setting or any existing test file. It adds one
census script, its suspects ledger and its pin test, and reports what they
measured. The script is deliberately wired into no workflow.

The card's original scope (the convention, plus a gate enforcing it) was withdrawn
by triage on 2026-09-10 after R51 measured 91 enumerating call sites in 23 files on
unmodified `main`; the written-down convention was refused in the same comment. Neither
was rebuilt.

---

## 1. The census

**Method.** Enumerate completed `CI` runs with `event=push` on the
`ci.yml` workflow, paging with explicit `&page=N` rather than `Link: rel="next"`
— objectui#6055 measured that cursor walking exhausts early and that is how that
card's own baseline denominator came out about a quarter short. Every run in the
window is `actor = github-merge-queue[bot]` and `run_attempt = 1`, so one push run
is one merge.

**The delivery probe is objectui#6055's: presence of the `coverage-report`
artifact. Never a run-level conclusion**, which objectui#6055 independently
re-confirmed is not a delivery proxy.

**The unit is a merge, not a run.** objectui#6049's per-sha concurrency group
cancels a superseded run and starts a fresh one on the same head sha seconds
later; the cancelled one carries no artifact and reads as red while the commit
got its merged report moments afterwards. Four such pairs are in the window.
Collapsing by sha is what makes this census agree with objectui#6055 to the unit.

**Denominator, objectui#6055's own window (2026-09-05 .. 2026-09-09T17:42Z):**

| reading | objectui#6055 | re-derived here |
|---|---|---|
| push-lane merges | 454 | **454** |
| red at the coverage gate | 301 | **301** |
| delivered | 152 | 153 |

**Denominator, the full census window (2026-09-02T08:53Z .. 2026-09-11T13:20Z):**
700 runs, 4 superseded, **696 merges, 343 red (49.3%)**.

**Cause split of the 301.**

| cause | merges | share |
|---|---|---|
| doc-links corpus walk — objectui#8419 | 196 | 65.1% |
| whole-repository scan — objectui#8479 / objectui#8380 | 54 | 17.9% |
| both instances red in the same merge | 29 | 9.6% |
| unattributed | 22 | 7.3% |

Over the full 696-merge window: 200 / 54 / 29 / 60 unattributed — **283 of 343 =
82.5%**.

## 2. The share that is this card's mechanism — 279 of 301 = 92.7%

**⛔ Not inferred from "it was red and something was slow."** Four independent
readings, each with its own control:

**(a) The red is an episode with two edges, and both edges are hoist commits.**
Red rate by segment, at merge granularity:

| segment | merges | red | rate |
|---|---|---|---|
| A — before `f7cf7e8a9f` (#7657, the change that grew the doc-links walk) | 117 | 5 | **4.3%** |
| B — `f7cf7e8a9f` .. `0203a29e9b` (the doc-links hoist, #8419) | 271 | 238 | **87.8%** |
| C — `0203a29e9b` .. `83d4fda160` (the unused-deps hoist, #8543) | 45 | 45 | **100.0%** |
| D — after both hoists | 263 | 55 | **20.9%** |

**(b) The failing shard is the shard the un-hoisted file computes into, on that
run's own tree.** `shardOf()` in the new script is a replica of vitest 4.1.10's
sequencer — sha1 of the root-relative spec path, sorted by digest, sliced by
`calculateShardRange`. It is validated, not asserted: against a real
`pnpm exec vitest run --shard=3/4 --project @object-ui/console` on `6214db63f` the
two file sets are identical, 24 of 24, empty in both directions; and
`specFilesFrom()` reproduces `pnpm exec vitest list --filesOnly` exactly, 2998
paths, zero in either direction.

| segment | red merges whose failing shard contains the live suspect |
|---|---|
| B (`check-doc-links.test.ts`) | **229 / 238** |
| C (`check-unused-dependencies.test.ts`) | **45 / 45** |
| A (same test, suspect not yet slow) | 1 / 5 |
| D (same test, suspect hoisted) | 36 / 59 |

⚠️ **That table on its own is weaker than it looks, and I would rather say so than
let it be read as stronger.** When one shard dominates a segment, "the failing shard
contains the suspect" approaches "that shard failed", which is nearly circular. The
discriminating form is the cross-segment one — **the suspect's shard never moves,
and its shard's failure rate does**:

| segment | merges | shard 2 failed | `check-doc-links` is in | shard 1 failed | `check-unused-dependencies` is in |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | 117 | 1 = **0.9%** | shard 2, all 117 trees | 0 = 0.0% | not in the tree |
| B | 271 | 229 = **84.5%** | shard 2, all 271 trees | 38 = 14.0% | absent for 233, then shard 1 |
| C | 45 | 4 = **8.9%** | shard 2, all 45 trees | 45 = **100.0%** | shard 1, all 45 |
| D | 263 | 32 = **12.2%** | shard 2, all 267 trees | 26 = 9.9% | shard 1, all 267 |

`check-doc-links.test.ts` computes into shard 2 in **every one of the 700 trees** and
never moves. Shard 2's failure rate goes 0.9% → 84.5% → 8.9%, rising at `f7cf7e8a9f`
and collapsing at `0203a29e9b`. The shard is the constant; the file's cost is the
variable.

⭐ And the second instance's onset is its own arrival, not drift:
`check-unused-dependencies.test.ts` is **added** by `0ea7054f80`
(2026-09-07T09:34:10Z, #8304), and the first push-lane merge with shard 1 red is
2026-09-07T09:52:35Z — **eighteen minutes later**. The tree listings agree
independently: the file is absent from the first 233 trees of segment B.

⚠️ Shallow-history caveat, stated because it bit once: this checkout's floor is
`ebb579dbbdee` (2026-08-09T21:29Z), and `git log --diff-filter=A` names exactly that
commit as the "creation" of `check-doc-links.test.ts` — a truncation artefact, ⛔ not
a reading, and it is not used anywhere above. Control legs:
`git cat-file -e FLOOR:scripts/__tests__/check-doc-links.test.ts` exits 0 (present at
the floor, so it predates the window) while the same for
`check-unused-dependencies.test.ts` exits 128 at both the floor and `0ea7054f80^`
(genuinely added there).

**(c) The uninstrumented lane ran the same split over the same files and did not
fail.** `ci.yml` gives `test` `if: github.event_name != 'push'` and `test-coverage`
`if: github.event_name == 'push'`, so the merge queue runs the identical 4-way
shard split without `--coverage`. Failed `merge_group` runs are trees that never
landed, so this comparison is **not** the tautology "everything that landed was
green":

| window | shard | `merge_group`, no coverage | push, with coverage |
|---|---|---|---|
| B | 2 (carries doc-links) | **0 / 358 = 0.0%** | **229 / 271 = 84.5%** |
| C | 1 (carries unused-deps) | **0 / 57 = 0.0%** | **45 / 45 = 100.0%** |
| B | 3 (control) | 0 / 358 | 0 / 271 |
| B | 4 (control) | 1 / 358 = 0.3% | 1 / 271 = 0.4% |
| C | 2 (control) | 4 / 57 = 7.0% | 4 / 45 = 8.9% |

Where the suspect is absent the two lanes agree to within two points. Where it is
present they differ by 84 and 100 points.

**(d) The instrumented cost, measured on the pre-hoist tree.** Checked out
`4b4d35a7d5` (`0203a29e9b^`) in a throwaway worktree and ran the file both ways:

| test | no coverage | with coverage | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| `…agrees with the real renderers…` | 3151 ms | **7814 ms** | 2.48x |
| `…has no setext headings…` | 2847 ms | **7301 ms** | 2.56x |
| whole file | 9.68 s | 17.68 s | 1.83x |

Against `testTimeout: 15000`, headroom falls from 4.8x to **1.92x**. Both legs were
green on this 4-core box — the timeout is load-dependent, which is exactly why
segment B is 87.8% red and not 100%.

**Is there a third instance in the 20.9% residual? NOT MEASURED, and ⛔ not "no".**
Eight candidate files — the card's own three slowest survivors, the two hoisted ones,
and three more whole-corpus walkers — were scored against segment D's 59 red merges by
the same shard test. Every one of them lands on 30/59 (50.8%) or 36/59 (61.0%), which
are exactly the marginal rates at which shards 1 and 2 failed in that segment: with
only two shards failing and all eight candidates living in one of them, the test has
no discriminating power there. That is a measurement returning "cannot tell", ⛔ not a
finding of absence. Settling it needs the failing-test names, which is objectui#9177.

## 3. The two premises the PM claim marked "not re-measured"

**Premise: same shards, same files, coverage instrumentation the only variable.**
**Substantially confirmed, with one correction.** Reading (c) is the empirical form
and reading (d) the mechanical one. The correction: the two lanes differ in four
ways, not one — `--coverage`, `--reporter=blob`, four `--coverage.thresholds.*=0`
overrides, and the non-push lane's `should_run` gate plus its `pnpm test:dist` step
on shard 1. Only `--coverage` changes execution cost; the rest are inert for
per-test timing. Also, the lane boundary is push versus *pull_request and
merge_group*, so the queue build is a second uninstrumented lane, which is what
makes reading (c) available at all.

**Premise: thresholds live only on the merged report, so one red shard means the
gate does not run.** **Confirmed, and now measured rather than quoted.** The shard
legs pass `--coverage.thresholds.lines=0 --coverage.thresholds.functions=0
--coverage.thresholds.branches=0 --coverage.thresholds.statements=0`
(`ci.yml:967-968`) against real thresholds of 40/33/30/40 (`vitest.config.mts:487`),
and every step of `coverage-report` up to its verdict is gated on
`needs.test-coverage.result == 'success'` (nine occurrences). Measured on all 347
artifact-absent runs, read from the check-run annotations the verdict step itself
emits:

- **347 / 347 say `Coverage gate did NOT run`**, every one with
  `blobs=skipped merge=skipped report=skipped`.
- **0 / 347 say `Coverage thresholds breached`.**

So across 696 merges the thresholds were evaluated on 353 commits and on 343 they
were never evaluated at all. ⛔ None of the red is a coverage regression.

## 4. What the card, triage and the PM claim got wrong

1. **The 66% is an episode, not a rate.** objectui#6055's window is almost exactly
   the epidemic. The baseline before it is 4.3% and the rate after both hoists is
   20.9%. The derived "82 of 125 push-lane runner-hours per day" was true of
   2026-09-05 .. 09-09 and is not true now. ⭐ The hypothesis is confirmed at a
   high share **and** the standing cost estimate is stale — both, not one.
2. **The card says "84 consecutive runs".** The block is **87** consecutive
   artifact-absent runs, 2026-09-07T09:36Z .. 2026-09-08T09:05Z.
3. **The mechanism is marginal, not binary.** "Green on every PR and red on every
   push" is exact for segment C (45/45) and wrong for segment B (238/271): at 2.5x
   instrumented cost the walk sits *at* the bound, so runner load decides. Two
   regimes, not one.
4. **The push lane cannot say why it is red, through any channel.** Measured
   directly: one throwaway file with one failing assertion and one deliberate
   timeout, run both ways on the same tree. Default reporter — exit 1, both test
   names, `Error: Test timed out in 50ms.`, `Tests 2 failed (2)`. `--reporter=blob`
   — exit 1, **one line of output**: `blob report written to …`. Two real red shard
   logs from `main` match that shape. The failures live in the `coverage-blob-N`
   artifact, which is download-only (`GET /actions/artifacts/ID/zip` and
   `GET /actions/jobs/ID/logs` both 302 to blob storage). **This is why an 87-run
   and an 84-run episode each had to be found by hand** — a separate and cheaper
   problem than the one the card was filed about. Filed bare as objectui#9177.
5. **The coverage contexts are not in the repo's own derived required set.** All 26
   entries of `REQUIRED_CONTEXTS` in `scripts/dependabot-merge-gate.mjs` name
   `Test (shard N/4)`; `Test (coverage)` and `Test (coverage shard N/4)` appear in
   none of them. Stated as what CI reported, ⛔ never as "required".

## 5. Gates

Exit codes captured before any pipe; each verdict line is the gate's own.

| gate | command | exit |
|---|---|---|
| new pin test | `pnpm exec vitest run scripts/__tests__/coverage-red-cause-census.test.ts` | 0 — `Test Files 1 passed (1) / Tests 20 passed (20) / Duration 632ms` |
| Type Check (scripts) | `pnpm type-check:scripts` | 0 |
| entry guard | `node scripts/check-entry-guard.mjs --self-test` then without | 0, 0 — `91 scripts/ file(s) … 0 file(s) still hand-type one` |
| lint coverage | `node scripts/check-lint-coverage.mjs` | 0 — `46/46 packages linted` |
| upstream port parity | `node scripts/check-upstream-port-parity.mjs` | 0 |
| type-check coverage | `node scripts/check-type-check-coverage.mjs` | 0 |
| pre-install import graph | `node scripts/check-pre-install-import-graph.mjs` | 0 |
| control bytes | `node scripts/check-control-bytes.mjs` | 0 — `scanned 7366 tracked text file(s)` |
| vi.mock override shape | `node scripts/check-vi-mock-override-shape.mjs` | 0 |
| shell escape residue | `node scripts/check-shell-escape-residue.mjs` | 0 |
| governed surface | `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` on the three paths | 0 — `NOT GOVERNED` |
| changeset | `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` | 0, verbatim below |

```
Compared the working tree with 6214db63f (merge-base with origin/main): 3 file(s) changed, 0 of them published source of a package the release covers, 0 of them a manifest whose published contract moved, 0 under a package changesets ignores, 0 changeset(s) added.
✅  No source or published contract of a released package changed in this range, so no changeset is owed.
```

**Lint, narrowed and declared.** `pnpm exec eslint --no-inline-config --format json`
on the two new JS/TS files: 2 files linted, **0 errors, 0 warnings**, exit 0 (the
`.json` ledger is not an eslint input). The narrowing is a measurement, not a skip:
`eslint.config.js` configures no `parserOptions.project` and no `projectService`
(`grep` exits 1), so linting is not type-aware and a file's verdict depends only on
its own bytes plus the flat config — three added files cannot move any untouched
file's verdict. The repo's own coverage authority agrees the population is intact:
`node scripts/check-lint-coverage.mjs` exits 0 with `46/46 packages linted, 0 with
outstanding errors`.

**The shard command CI runs.** The new pin test computes into shard 1 of 4 on this
tree, so shard 1 is the one owed. Run locally, verbatim:
`pnpm test:coverage --reporter=blob --shard=1/4 --coverage.thresholds.lines=0 --coverage.thresholds.functions=0 --coverage.thresholds.branches=0 --coverage.thresholds.statements=0`
— **exit 0**, about 15 minutes. ⚠️ Worth recording what the green run *printed*,
because it corroborates objectui#9177 from the other side: 1459 lines / 118 KB, of
which lines 1-115 are stdout the tests themselves emitted, line 115 is `blob report
written to …`, and 116-1459 are the v8 coverage **text** table. **Zero lines of
vitest's own test summary.** And a red shard exits before that table is generated, so
a red log has neither the failure summary nor the coverage table — exactly the shape
of the two real red shard logs sampled from `main`.

**What CI reported: nothing yet.** This draft PR is opened at report time, so its
checks are `in_progress`. Everything above is a local run of the command CI runs.

## 6. Post-merge probe — tree reads only

No runner leg: every command below is `git` or `sha256sum` and runs in a bare
checkout with no `node_modules`.

```
git show --stat MERGE_SHA                      # 3 files, 595 insertions, 0 deletions
git show MERGE_SHA:scripts/coverage-red-cause-census.mjs | sha256sum
git show MERGE_SHA:scripts/__tests__/coverage-red-cause-census.test.ts | sha256sum
git show MERGE_SHA:scripts/coverage-red-cause-suspects.json | sha256sum
git grep -c "check-doc-links.test.ts" MERGE_SHA -- scripts/coverage-red-cause-suspects.json
git grep -n "coverage.thresholds.lines=0" MERGE_SHA -- .github/workflows/ci.yml
git grep -c "needs.test-coverage.result == 'success'" MERGE_SHA -- .github/workflows/ci.yml
git grep -n "testTimeout" MERGE_SHA -- vitest.config.mts
git show -s --format=%s 0203a29e9b 83d4fda160 f7cf7e8a9f
git show --stat --format= 0203a29e9b
```

Expected, as measured on the branch tip before push:

```
0333b1e9b18bbc5b3e68c4a84bfd71f11803463c0830d6f2d5e55b762827d71e  census script
57f470170775b4e68ae8a5c20e1a8af0143a2fb2d331c7d896faed316632b162  pin test
12e1f45d7abd3d4e9b414f21cb98996b06874729ae2d39526c71a4f4d10cc78b  suspects ledger
ci.yml:967    --coverage.thresholds.lines=0 --coverage.thresholds.functions=0
ci.yml        9 occurrences of needs.test-coverage.result == 'success'
vitest.config.mts:282    testTimeout: 15000,
0203a29e9b  test(scripts): hoist the doc-links corpus walk out of the timed window (#8419)
83d4fda160  test(scripts): hoist the whole-repository scan out of check-unused-dependencies' timed window (#8543)
f7cf7e8a9f  fix(scripts): check-doc-links resolves the #fragment, not just the file (objectui#7644) (#7657)
0203a29e9b  scripts/__tests__/check-doc-links.test.ts | 174 +++++-------  (104 insertions, 70 deletions)
```

Two probe legs are **dev-only, ⛔ not run by the PM** because they need a runner:
the shard replica validation against a real `vitest run --shard=3/4` (24 of 24,
empty both ways) and the instrumented-cost table in section 2(d). Their readings
from this seat's run are quoted above.

## 7. Reproducing the census

```
NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1 node scripts/coverage-red-cause-census.mjs --fetch --since=2026-09-02 > snap.json
node scripts/coverage-red-cause-census.mjs --snapshot=snap.json
```

`NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1` is load-bearing on a proxied host: Node's built-in `fetch`
ignores `HTTPS_PROXY` and `--fetch` answers 403 on the first page, which reads
exactly like a permissions problem. The `--snapshot` path needs no network.
